data.about_me: Bill McCann has been the Host of "The Saturday Morning Edition of Jazz" on WCDB since April of 1985. This weekly jazz program airs Live on Saturday mornings from 8 am until Noon. It is also rebroadcast on Sundays from 10 am until 2 pm. April 2025 will mark the 40th Anniversary of Bill's hosting of this award-winning program. To mark the occasion and to celebrate Jazz Appreciation Month, there will be a full day of Jazz at the University at Albany on Saturday, April 5, 2025, beginning at noon. "The UAlbany Jazz Appreciation Month Festival, Celebrating Bill McCann's 40th Anniversary on WCDB" will be held on the Uptown Campus of the University at Albany, on 2 stages in the Campus Center West building. The Festival will feature 16 jazz bands comprised of over 80 of the finest jazz musicians from the Capital District and beyond. Free Commemorative T-Shirts (While Supplies Last) and thanks to the folks at The Saratoga Performing Arts Center (SPAC) we will be having a free raffle for pairs of tickets to this Summer's Saratoga Jazz Festival, Presented by G.E. Verona, on June 28th and 29th. (You must be present to enter). More information can be found at https://wcdb.org/jazz Note: Sets are @ 50 minutes with a 10 minute changeover. ORB STAGE: starts at Noon. Noon: -Bossamba: Maggie MacDougall, vocals; Wayne Hawkins, keys; Lou Pappas, bass; Mark Foster, drums. 1 pm: The GNP Trio: Tyler Giroux, keys; Dylan Perrillo, bass; Matt Niedbalski, drums. 2 pm: -The Arch Stanton Quartet: Roger Noyes, guitar; Terry Gordon, trumpet; Chris Macchia, bass; James Ketterer, drums. 3 pm: -The Teresa Broadwell Quartet: Teresa Broadwell, vocals/violin; Leo Russo, sax; Michael Novakowski, guitar; Pete Toigo, bass. 4 pm: -The Justin Henricks Trio: Justin Henricks, guitar; Ian MacDonald, organ; Nick Anderson, drums. 5 pm: -The Awan Rashad Quartet: Awan Rashad, sax; Luke Franco, guitar; Tarik Shah, bass; Matt Niedbalski, drums. 6 pm: -The Pete Levin Organ Trio: Pete Levin, organ; Steve Raleigh, guitar; Cliff Brucker, drums. 7 pm: -The Chuck Lamb Trio: Chuck Lamb, keys; Rich Syracuse, bass; Jeff "Siege" Siegel, drums. MULTI-PURPOSE ROOM STAGE: starts at 12:45 pm 12:45 pm: -The Steel Pier Jazz Band: Woody Strobeck, trombone; Dave Lambert, clarinet; Steve Lambert, trumpet; Glenn Hankle, banjo; Ernie Belanger, tuba; Jeff McRae, drums. 1:45 pm: -The Linda Brown Jazz Project: Linda Brown, bass; Jody Shayne, vocals; Larry Ham, keys; Laura Andrea Leguia, sax; Jeff "Siege" Siegel, drums. 2:45 pm: -Michael Benedict Jazz Vibes with the Art D'echo Trio: Michael Benedict, vibes; David Gleason, keys; Mike Lawrence, bass and Pete Sweeney, drums; plus Joe Finn, guitar; and Brian Melick, percussion. 3:45: -The Keith Pray Soul Jazz Revival: Keith Pray, sax; Pat Perkinson, bass; Vinnie Martucci, keys; Doug Bierend, guitar; Bob Halek, drums. 4:45 pm: -Colleen Pratt / Peg Delaney Ensemble: Colleen Pratt, vocals; Peg Delaney, keys; Bill Delaney, bass and Gene Garone, drums; Jim Corigliano, sax and Steve Lambert, trumpet and flugelhorn. 5:45 pm: -Joe Barna and Sketches of Influence: Joe Barna, drums; Stacy Dillard, sax; Greg Glassman, Trumpet; Ian MacDonald, keys and Malik McLaurine, bass. 6:45 pm: -The Brian Patneaude Quintet: Brian Patneaude, sax; Rob Lindquist, keys; Justin Henricks, guitar; Jarod Grieco, bass and Danny Welchel, drums. 7:45 pm: -The B.W.C. Jazz Orchestra: 18 piece big band lead by Cliff Brucker, Steve Weisse and Dylan Canterbury. Featuring: Jim Corigliano, Paul Evoskevich, Dave Fisk, Kevin Barcomb, Kaitlyn Fay (+ vocals), Wally Johnson - Saxes; Steve Weisse, Chris Pasin, Kathleen Ehlinger, Nikola Tomic- Trumpets; Ben O’Shea, Rick Rosoff, Travis Malone, Shaun Bazylewicz - Trombones; Jon LeRoy - piano Dave Shoudy - bass Cliff Brucker - drums Dylan Canterbury - trumpet, conductor. The event is free and open to the public thanks to the generous support of the following Sponsors: The UAlbany Alumni Association; The UAlbany Foundation; The University Auxiliary Services at Albany (UAS); The UAlbany Division of Student Affairs and Enrollment; The Albany Musicians Union, Local 14 of the American Federation of Musicians; The Schenectady-Amsterdam Musical Union, Local 85-133 of the American Federation of Musicians; The Music Performance Trust Fund; The Nania Family - In Memory of Sheldon and Carol Pitkin; Canon Kay C. Hotaling; A Place for Jazz; and WCDB. Free Commemorative T-Shirts (while supplies last). And thanks to the folks up at The Saratoga Performing Arts Center, we will be giving away pairs of tickets to the Saratoga Jazz Festival, Presented by GE Verona, taking place on June 28th and 29th. You must be present to win! Bill received the prestigious "Jazz Hero" Award from the Jazz Journalists Association in 2012(the JJA) https://www.jjajazzawards.org/p/jazz-heroes.html. He was also named "Best Jazz D.J." on several occasions by "The Metroland" - the newly reborn weekly arts publication in the Capital District of New York. In recognition of his radio efforts, Bill has been nominated for an "Eddies" Award on several occasions. In addition to his serving as Host and Jazz Director at WCDB, Bill has been very active in the Jazz Community in the Capital District. He is presently President and a member of the Board of Directors of "A Place for Jazz" and has served as a Board Member for many years. A Place for Jazz is a 501(c)(3) not-for-profit corporation dedicated to promoting Jazz in the Capital District, and beyond. (aplaceforjazz.org) Bill is also a member of the Swingtime Jazz Society, a membership-based organization having as it's sole purpose the promotion of good music by sponsoring open-to-the-public concerts that feature regional jazz artists. (swingtimejazz.org)

data.comments: The Maiden Voyage has returned to the airwaves of the capital district after 25 years. Maiden Voyage started at the SUNYA Campus radio cable station WSUA in 1971 and later moved to WMHT-FM from 1975-77. The Voyage hosted by O. J. or Dr. Joseph Bowman, Jr., brings a contemporary mix of jazz, R&B, Afro Cuban, and World music to the capital district audiences. O. J. is a professor in the Department of Educational Theory and Practice, School of Education at the University at Albany with an interest in technology and how it is used in society. Radio is a technology that has been around for a long time and provides communities with rich resources and information. The main focus of the music is jazz but because jazz has influenced music the world over, I share these influences with my audiences. You will hear different music on the show but always remember that it is based on the jazz experience. I always feature artists that do not get the air-play they deserve and keep them in the listening ears of the audience. The Maiden Voyage brings years of jazz experience to the capital region and will share the work of the old and new jazz musicians with the audience. We are presently on Thursdays from 4-6 PM at WCDB-FM, 90.9 FM and can be heard on the internet at wcdb.albany.edu. If you want more information about O. J. please visit www.albany.edu/cuyt or send e-mail to jebowman@albany.edu

data.about_me: DJ ShOw would be the first to tell you that his love for music started at home and a gift has been passed down through his family for generations. As a kid, music was always constant no matter where he was, at his house, or for any occasion or none at all—music was everywhere. As an eight year old, ShOw officially fell in love with music, and being around DJs since that age, a new DJ inevitably emerged—DJ ShOw. He would always take notes and was willing to help at any and every opportunity. Aside from his bloodline's influence, DJ ShOw especially cites DJ Joey O, who introduced him to the art and technique of djing, as a mentor and an inspiration. His other influences include Kid Capri, DJ Ron G, Funkmaster Flex, Kool DJ Red Alert, DJ Precise, DJ S&S, to name a few. For ShOw, who has always been ambitious, inspirations led to aspirations, and in the eighth grade, he began DJing as a hobby. On his 13th birthday, this hobby evolved into a career option when his father brought him his first set of turntables and a mixer. A short year later, ShOw was spinning at various house parties, a routine that would undoubtedly expand. When he graduated high school with honors, ShOw decided to further his studies at the State University of New York at Albany—where he is currently pursuing his B.A. in Communications and Business. It was at Albany where DJ ShOw's progress continued as he co-founded Money Talks Entertainment with good friend DJ Playboy, who held the position of Urban Director at the SUNY Albany station, 90.9 WCDB. Naturally, ShOw displayed interest and began helping DJ Playboy during his shows, and at the end of his first semester, Money Talks Entertainment was formed. Immediately the duo went to work, producing and distributing two mixtapes throughout the Capital Region, The Takeover Hip-Hop Series and Grown and Sexy R&B Series. Not too long afterwards, MTE recruited a third member of the crew, DJ Sunkiss. Together, the three NYC-bred DJs overtook and dominated the Albany DJ scene. Since, the MTE trio has orchestrated a reggae mixtape to their collection, The Pull It Up reggae mixtape series has been distributed both locally and over the internet, launching the company's potential to a worldwide level. Today, the MTE Co-Founder and C.E.O. hosts his own radio show every Wed. night at 8 p.m. on WCDB 90.9, which also broadcasts live online at www.WCDBfm.com. Additionally, DJ ShOw is also a part of the DJ crew the Knockout Kingz and is the official DJ for independent record label Bottomline Entertainment and their flagship artist Rover. Money Talks Entertainment is: DJ ShOw, DJ Sunkiss, DJ Playboy, 'Ms. Perfect Touch' Nish, & DJ Phayda G

I'm still a DJ at WMTU 91.9 FM Houghton, so be sure to listen in at www.wmtu.mtu.edu I'm mostly famous nowadays for being a kite aerial photographer. Check out my work at Kite Aerial Photography with Nathan Invincible for some sweet pictures of the Upper Peninsula of Michigan and beyond.
data.comments: I did 4 years of radio during my undergraduate career at WMTU. WMTU was a freeform station, so people played what they wanted without restrictions. I'm back there now after 2 years at WCDB, so catch my show every Thursday night from 8-10 PM at WMTU 91.9 FM Houghton. I'm a current DJ there, check me out Thursdays 8-10 PM on WMTU.Notable Things I've Done: I currently hold the record for the longest known radio show at WCDB at 36 hours straight.I played nearly 4 hours of Thriller covers and remixes for Halloween 2011.To find new electronic music, I would play albums I'd never heard before based solely on the color of the artwork.  A different color ever show!13 shows in one month (October 2011), more than most DJs do over a semester.

data.interests: For a piece of music to be considered a song in its true sense, it should be held to the same standards as a literary or cinematic work, or any other form of art that is presented over time.  Any work in the field of "composed art" may be reasonably expected to conform to such basic protocols as having a beginning, middle, and end, and having a central theme or other overarching device which ensures coherence throughout.  Once this standard is established, Any piece that falls short of these basic criteria can be logically and comfortably classified as experimentation.  As in all forms of art, there is a place for experimentation--even a glorious one; however, every experiment must be evaluated as such: successes should be praised, failures should be rejected, and new possibilities should be pursued by those who have the heart to do so.

data.about_me: Hi, I’m Jeff, one of the new community DJs. I was a college radio guy at Penn State in the late 80s/early 90s and I’m super psyched to jump back into it 30+ years later!As a kid in the early 80s I would listen to the top 30 countdown on the radio every week and write it down in a notebook. I discovered metal in 1985 and quickly fell in love with thrash metal in particular. While doing college radio I got to experience the first wave of death metal and the explosion of “grunge” in real time, which was amazing. My musical horizons also expanded greatly and I discovered countless awesome bands and genres I wouldn’t have discovered otherwise. I listen to a little bit of everything and believe that there’s something interesting about every single genre and subgenre out there. I especially admire genre-bending artists that are hard to pigeonhole and aren't afraid to take risks. Anyway, I’m rambling. You get the idea!
